finding: All 30 z-reference, case-definition and probe-collapse sensitivity rows retained their expected module direction.
interpretation_boundary: Direction preservation does not imply identical effect magnitude or statistical significance.

finding: GSE72810 sensitivity-score concordance remained high; minimum Pearson r = 0.9874322 and minimum Spearman rho = 0.9813714.
interpretation_boundary: Correlation measures score-level concordance and does not replace effect-size comparison.

finding: VIR_M2 retained a viral-higher direction but lost confidence-interval and FDR support under GSVA in both z-reference populations.
interpretation_boundary: VIR_M2 should be described as scoring-method-sensitive rather than uniformly robust across scoring algorithms.

finding: BACT_M1 was borderline under mean-z scoring but gained confidence-interval and FDR support under GSVA.
interpretation_boundary: The stronger GSVA result does not convert BACT_M1 into a uniformly supported module across all primary analyses.

finding: All 29826 leave-one/two-gene variants retained the expected direction; minimum Pearson r with the complete module was 0.9940203.
interpretation_boundary: Deletion robustness supports distributed module signal but does not establish causal sufficiency of individual genes.
